operations.before:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Every isogeny f:A→C has dual isogeny f^vee:C^vee→A^vee whose kernel is (kerf)^D as a group scheme and whose degree equals degf. The canonical Poincare morphism kappa:A→A^{vee vee} is an isomorphism; dual pullback is contravariantly functorial on homomorphisms and additive for parallel homomorphisms f,g:A→C. Complete proof strategy: For an isogeny f:A→C with kernel H, f is the fppf quotient. A rigidified bundle M on C_T with f^*M trivial descends the trivial bundle on A_T with H_T-action. Universal constants force any such action to be a character H_T→Gm,T. Trivializations differ only by a base unit, so the character is independent of choice; conversely character descent produces M. Tensor and base change commute with the construction. All these bundles are in Pic0: the finite-flat norm makes M^(deg f) trivial, and a torsion class has φ_M=0 because [deg f] is an epimorphism. Hence ker f^∨=H^D **as group schemes**, with no reduced-kernel restriction. Finite rank equality gives deg f^∨=deg f; dimension and finite kernel give an isogeny.

Switching the normalized Poincaré bundle defines κ_A:A→B^∨. Symmetry of Λ(L) gives φ_L=φ_L^∨κ_A on every test. Its finite kernel makes κ_A an isogeny. Degree equality for φ_L and its dual then gives deg κ_A=1, so κ_A is an isomorphism. Pullback of normalized bundles gives contravariance and composition; the cube identity gives (f+g)^vee=f^vee+g^vee for homomorphisms f,g:A→C with a common source and target.
operations.after:
Assume AC and DC as inherited from the supplied scheme and cohomology results. Every isogeny f:A→C (a surjective homomorphism with finite scheme-theoretic kernel) has dual isogeny f^vee:C^vee→A^vee whose kernel is (kerf)^D as a group scheme and whose degree equals degf. The canonical Poincare morphism kappa:A→A^{vee vee} is an isomorphism; dual pullback is contravariantly functorial on homomorphisms and additive for parallel homomorphisms f,g:A→C. Complete proof strategy: For an isogeny f:A→C with kernel H, f is the fppf quotient. A rigidified bundle M on C_T with f^*M trivial descends the trivial bundle on A_T with H_T-action. Universal constants force any such action to be a character H_T→Gm,T. Trivializations differ only by a base unit, so the character is independent of choice; conversely character descent produces M. Tensor and base change commute with the construction. All these bundles are in Pic0: the character is killed by d=rank H, so its d-th tensor descent datum is trivial and M^d is rigidified-trivial. Hence d·φ_M=0. The pointed morphism φ_M into finite affine C^vee[d]_T factors through T by universal structure sections, and its factor is zero; thus φ_M=0 on every test. Hence ker f^∨=H^D **as group schemes**, with no reduced-kernel restriction. Finite rank equality gives deg f^∨=deg f; dimension and finite kernel give an isogeny.

Switching the normalized Poincaré bundle defines κ_A:A→B^∨. Symmetry of Λ(L) gives φ_L=φ_L^∨κ_A on every test. Its finite kernel makes κ_A an isogeny. Degree equality for φ_L and its dual then gives deg κ_A=1, so κ_A is an isomorphism. Pullback of normalized bundles gives contravariance and composition; the cube identity gives (f+g)^vee=f^vee+g^vee for homomorphisms f,g:A→C with a common source and target.



The Poincare pullback (id_A times phi_L)^*P_A is on A times A. Comparing the defining dual pullback with the switched Poincare bundle gives phi_L=phi_L^vee composed with kappa_A using the symmetry of the normalized square family; no ill-typed A times A^vee pullback is used. Projectivity supplies the ample L.
